# ARM Semantic Review

The ARM API Reviewer is an AI agent. Auto-signoff must not trust it directly, so its verdict is
turned into one **commit status**, `ARM Semantic Review`, on the reviewed SHA. Universal
Auto-Signoff reads that status alongside LintDiff and Avocado.

Short overview next to the code:
[README.md](../../workflows/src/arm-auto-signoff/README.md).

## Mental model

```text
START   pre_activation          post status PENDING, upload one head-sha=<sha>;issue-number=<n> artifact
MIDDLE  agent (read-only AI)    review the PR, then request record_arm_semantic_review
END     record job (trusted)    validate the 4 values, post SUCCESS / FAILURE / ERROR
SAFETY  conclusion job          if no result was posted, turn this run's PENDING into ERROR
READ    Universal Auto-Signoff  re-check the PR is open at the evaluated head, read the newest status
                                on that SHA plus labels -> label action
APPLY   Update Labels           add or remove the label as emitted
```

The model proposes. Trusted code validates and publishes. Any doubt ends as "not Passed".

| File                                                                                                    | Role                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| [arm-semantic-review.ts](../../workflows/src/arm-auto-signoff/arm-semantic-review.ts)                   | Pure policy: validate the result, map it to a status, read statuses. No I/O. |
| [arm-semantic-review-workflow.ts](../../workflows/src/arm-auto-signoff/arm-semantic-review-workflow.ts) | I/O: publish the status, finalize an unpublished one.                        |

| [context.ts](../../workflows/src/context.ts)                                                            | `extractInputs` and the trusted-artifact parser shared by all consumers.     |

## The status contract

Context `ARM Semantic Review`, bound to the reviewed SHA. `target_url` is
`.../actions/runs/<id>/attempts/<n>`, which identifies the run that wrote it.

| State     | Description starts with    | Meaning                                         | Adds `ARMManualSignoffRequired`? |
| --------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `pending` | `ARM API semantic review`  | Review in progress                              | No                               |
| `success` | `Passed:`                  | Full, complete review, 0 Blocking findings      | No                               |
| `failure` | `Changes requested:`       | Full, complete review with Blocking findings    | No                               |
| `error`   | `Manual review required: ` | Scoped review, or `specification/` over the cap | **Yes**                          |
| `error`   | `Review incomplete: `      | Failed, cancelled, unreadable, or unvalidated   | No                               |

Only `success` can lead to signoff. The two `error` outcomes share a state and are told apart by
the description prefix, so keep the prefixes in `arm-semantic-review.ts` as the single source.
`Manual review required` is a property of the PR. `Review incomplete` is transient, so a re-run
can still pass and it must never add the sticky label.

## Validation, and why each check exists

Trusted inputs (never from the model): the PR number and head SHA come from the run's correlation
artifact, named `head-sha=<sha>;issue-number=<n>` (`;` joins the pairs so one upload carries both),
and the attempt from `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`.

| Check                                                                         | Where                                  | If it fails               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Trusted artifacts present, full 40-hex SHA, no conflicting duplicates         | `context.ts`                           | Nothing published / throw |
| Output file exists and is JSON                                                | publisher `try`                        | `Review incomplete`       |
| Exactly one `record_arm_semantic_review` item                                 | `parseSemanticReviewResult`            | `Review incomplete`       |
| `blocking_count` is a digit string; the other three fields are in closed sets | `parseSemanticReviewResult`            | `Review incomplete`       |
| A `complete` review must have reason `none`                                   | `parseSemanticReviewResult`            | `Review incomplete`       |
| PR size within the cap, checked independently of the model's `scope`          | `requiresManualReview` (workflow file) | `Manual review required`  |
| Incomplete, then scoped, then Blocking, then Passed (first match wins)        | `evaluateSemanticReview`               | n/a                       |

### Verifying the model's scope

The model reports `scope: full|scoped`, but it is untrusted. For a **full, complete** claim, the
trusted code re-derives scope with the reviewer prompt's rule: more than 50 `specification/` files
or 5,000 `specification/` lines needs a human. The rules are pure helpers in
`arm-semantic-review.ts` (`checkPullRequestSize` and `addSpecificationChanges`); the workflow file's
`getOversizeReason` does the API calls and logging. Any other claim (scoped, incomplete) already
withholds signoff, so the check is skipped.

1. Zero changed files (GitHub could not compute the diff) or 3,000 or more requires manual review
   without listing files. 3,000 is the most files GitHub's file-listing API will return, so a PR
   that large cannot be proven fully covered.
2. If the PR's totals are within the cap, its `specification/` subset is too: no file list, so
   most PRs cost one `pulls.get` call.
3. Otherwise count only the `specification/` files, and stop paginating as soon as the count is
   over the cap. A renamed or moved file counts when either its old or its new path is under
   `specification/`.

The status says why, for example `Manual review required: specification/ changes exceed 50 files
or 5000 lines`. Reasons are fixed strings, never model output. Each step logs what it saw.
Deliberately **not** validated, because it adds code without protecting signoff:

- the PR being open or still at the reviewed SHA (the status is SHA-bound and Universal re-checks
  the live head);
- a "newer run exists" check before publishing (a late same-SHA write is stale but valid for that
  SHA);
- re-validating the attempt, PR, or SHA inside the parser (already validated upstream).

Error text from a failed validation goes to the run log only. The published description is the
fixed string `Review incomplete: result could not be validated`, so runner paths and API errors
never reach a public status.

## Invariants: do not break these

1. The model never supplies the SHA, PR number, or attempt.
2. Only `success` authorizes signoff; every unknown, missing, or errored case is "not Passed".
3. `statuses: write` stays in trusted jobs only (`pre_activation`, the record job, `conclusion`).
   Never give it to the `agent` job, and Universal stays `statuses: read`.
4. The finalizer publishes only when this exact run and attempt owns the newest `pending` status.
5. `Review incomplete` never adds `ARMManualSignoffRequired`.
6. Do not check out or run PR code in any of these jobs (`pull_request_target`).

## Behavior in the edge cases

| Situation                                                    | Result                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| New commit pushed during a review                            | An eligible push cancels the run (`cancel-in-progress`). The old SHA's status is never read for the new head. |
| `/arm-review` while a run is in flight                       | Cancels the old run and starts a new one on the same SHA.                                                     |
| Agent `noop`, failure, timeout, detection failure, or cancel | The `conclusion` finalizer turns this run's `pending` into `Review incomplete`.                               |
| Transient GitHub API error while publishing                  | `Review incomplete`, no sticky label. A re-run can pass.                                                      |
| Critic unavailable                                           | `Review incomplete: critic-unavailable`, labels unchanged.                                                    |
| Scoped or oversized PR                                       | `Manual review required`, adds `ARMManualSignoffRequired`.                                                    |
| Non-team-member actor                                        | No `pending`, no artifacts, no status. Signoff stays blocked.                                                 |
| Event the gate skips (other label, other comment)            | The run is skipped. Those events get a private concurrency lane so they cannot cancel a review.               |

## Known limitations

- Update Labels applies the emitted label action without re-checking the PR head. Universal checks
  just before emitting, so a push in the short window between the two can leave the pilot label
  stale until the next evaluation. A stale-head guard in Update Labels is a separate, cross-cutting
  change (it affects every producer that publishes a `head-sha=` artifact).
- A same-SHA re-run posts `pending` but does not revoke an existing `ARMAutoSignedOff-Test`
  label until Universal next runs. This matters only once enforcement is on.
- Universal's label filter does not include `ARMChangesRequested` or `WaitForARMFeedback`, so
  adding them does not trigger an immediate re-evaluation.
- The newest status named `ARM Semantic Review` wins; its creator is not verified.
- If a re-run resolves a different head SHA than the first attempt, two `head-sha=` artifacts can
  conflict and the parser throws, which can leave `Pending`.
- `blocking_count` is the model's verdict. The Critic and threat detection are the only checks on
  it, which is an accepted trade-off.
- A `Pending` status is resolved in almost every failure, but can still remain when the
  `conclusion` job does not run, the finalizer's own API calls still fail after their retries,
  the runner or GitHub is lost mid-run, or the finalizer cannot read the head SHA (the
  conflicting-artifacts case above). Nothing signs off in any of these cases, because only
  `success` does.
- A push to a draft PR, or to one without `WaitForARMFeedback`, joins the PR concurrency lane
  before the gate skips it, so it can cancel a review that is already running.

## Changing the reviewer workflow

1. Edit `arm-api-review.md`, then regenerate the lock file with the same gh-aw version recorded in
   the lock file header (`gh aw compile arm-api-review`). Confirm `git diff` shows only intended
   changes. The compiler may also prune unrelated entries in `.github/aw/actions-lock.json`;
   revert those.
2. A custom job cannot run after the agent: gh-aw rejects it as a dependency cycle. Post-agent
   work goes in the built-in `conclusion` job via `jobs.conclusion.pre-steps`.
3. `pre_activation` is the only place that can post `pending` before the agent starts.
4. Keep the concurrency expression and the `if:` trigger gate consistent.
5. The size cap exists in the prompt (Trigger Validation) and in `arm-semantic-review.ts`. Change
   both together.

## Verify a change

```bash
cd .github
npx vitest run workflows/test/arm-auto-signoff workflows/test/arm-api-review-workflow.test.ts workflows/test/context.test.ts
npx tsc --noEmit
npx oxlint workflows
npx oxfmt --check workflows
```

The tests assert the compiled lock file (job order, permissions, the finalizer condition), so a
stale lock file fails them.

Live check on a test PR (ideally in `azure-rest-api-specs-pr`), then compare to the tables above:

```bash
gh api repos/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/commits/<head-sha>/statuses \
  --jq '.[] | select(.context=="ARM Semantic Review") | [.created_at,.state,.description,.target_url]'
```

The `pending` status and the `head-sha=<sha>;issue-number=<n>` artifact appear on the run created
by `pre_activation`. Try: a clean review, `skip-arm-review`, a push mid-run, two `/arm-review`
comments in a row, and cancelling a run.

## Debug a status that is stuck or wrong

1. List the statuses for the head SHA (command above). Which `target_url` is newest, and is it
   the run you expect?
2. Open that run. Did `record_arm_semantic_review` run? It needs the agent and detection to
   succeed and an emitted `record_arm_semantic_review` item.
3. If it did not run, check whether the `conclusion` finalizer step ran. It is skipped when the
   record job succeeded, and it acts only on a `pending` this exact run owns.
4. If the description is `Review incomplete: result could not be validated`, read the warning in
   the record job's log for the real reason.
5. If Universal did not act, check its run log: it prints the event, correlation, labels, and the
   status it read. A "state/head mismatch" means the PR head moved on.
